fact: President Ruto announced the Digital Superhighway's 100,000km national fibre target in November 2022 for universal broadband availability over five years, with a deadline of 2027 that the 2 September 2026 report says is still ahead, and no successor named.

The Digital Superhighway fibre programme is funded through the Universal Service Fund, with the CA and ICT Authority initially signing a Sh5 billion agreement covering 19 counties, and Kenya Power had received Sh940.6 million by June 2025 for design, supply and installation, per the Daily Nation.

The FY2026/27 budget allocates Sh1.3 billion to maintain the national fibre backbone, Sh400 million for digital hubs and Sh382 million for digital superhighway cybersecurity, which Business Daily describes as part of the Digital Superhighway agenda to lay 100,000km of fibre.
Techweez says the National Broadband Strategy 2025-2030 puts Kenya's current fibre at 40,000km and sets a 100,000km target.
